newsitem.title: UK: Police contain trouble with activists in London.
newsitem.headline: Police contain trouble with activists in London.

text.p: Police and environmental activists battled on the streets of central London on Saturday after a march calling for greater social justice turned violent outside the gates of Prime Minister John Major's residence.
Police said at least four officers were injured when demonstrators bombarded them with cans, paint, planks of wood and smoke bombs at the entrance to Major's Downing Street office.

Several arrests were made as police donned riot gear and called in reinforcements on horseback and pushed the protesters back to Trafalgar Square where the main bulk of the marchers had arrived peacefully for a rally highlighting disparities in living standards.
The rally later turned festive with pop music blaring from speakers in the square and marchers holding "Reclaim the Streets" banners danced and sat in the streets blocking traffic.

A police spokeswoman said trouble flared when a group of about 500 activists among the estimated 7,000-strong march harangued police standing behind barriers and then tried to climb the gates leading to Downing Street.
Eyewitnesses said windows were broken in a nearby McDonalds hamburger restaurant and animal rights activists chanted slogans outside.

Police said about 7,000 people -- including the unemployed, disabled people, pensioners and asylum seekers -- took part in a march organised by dockers from the northwestern port of Liverpool who were sacked in a long-running industrial dispute.

"Direct action" groups have emerged in Britain over the past five years. Their high-profile tactics rang from living in tree houses to stop new road-building schemes, moving in on derelict land to highlight housing shortages and digging holes in motorways.
The activists had warned they planned a "spectacular event" during the march and police had been on alert for trouble.
